generatedFor: ACS I-595 Safety Twin — Demo Case Validation
note: Every record in this file is SYNTHETIC. It exists to demonstrate how the incident → inspection → repair → QC/QA → claim lifecycle is validated when a complete record set exists, which the real ACS and DataConnect exports do not yet provide. No inspection, repair, QC/QA or claim in this file happened. Personnel, work orders, claim references and photographs are invented and prefixed DEMO- so they cannot be mistaken for production records. Only the LOCATION of each case is real: it is taken from an existing I-595 incident in the corridor's own register at runtime, and the synthetic damage described here did not occur at that location.
assumptions: Stage statuses shown in the application are DERIVED from the field data below by the shared validation engine. The declaredStatus on each stage is the demo narrative's own claim and is asserted against the derived value by the unit tests; it is never what the screen displays.

Where an ACS QC/QA checklist states no numeric tolerance, no tolerance has been invented. Thresholds carried here are quoted from the checklist itself (and name the clause). The one demonstration-only threshold is marked `demonstrationOnly: true` and is labelled as an assumption on screen.

Each case declares the ACS QC/QA checklist it was inspected against. The existing selection engine is still run and its own choice is reported beside the declared one, so a disagreement is visible rather than hidden.

Evidence recovery: only the DataConnect connector queries real data. Office Track, MIMS and SunGuide have no endpoint or credentials in this deployment, so their responses are deterministic synthetic stand-ins answered from this file, stamped synthetic on every record and never presented as API results.

Incident context: weather is a real Open-Meteo historical reading. No timestamped speed, volume or congestion observation exists for this corridor in any connected system, so those are synthetic and labelled; the lane-closure, injury and fatality flags and the segment AADT are real and are attributed to the source incident and the FDOT network.
